claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a homogeneous, single-phase simple solid solution by standard solution treatment.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in this homogeneous solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The homogeneous equimolar alloy lacks nanoscale precipitates or short-range-ordered regions that effectively obstruct dislocations.
The equimolar homogeneous state has low lattice distortion.
Low lattice distortion and the absence of microstructural obstacles allow dislocations to glide with minimal resistance.
Relatively easy dislocation glide produces lower hardness and compressive strength while preserving favorable plasticity.
A slight excess of Ti can promote nanoscale precipitates or short-range order in near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
A tailored heat treatment can promote nanoscale precipitates or short-range order without grossly altering the CoCrFeNiTi matrix.
Nanoscale precipitates or short-range-ordered regions pin or obstruct dislocations.
Dislocation obstruction by the induced nanoscale heterogeneities increases hardness.
Dislocation obstruction by the induced nanoscale heterogeneities increases compressive strength.
Strengthening by the induced nanoscale heterogeneities reduces compressive plastic strain.
The predicted increase in hardness and compressive strength and reduction in plastic strain will occur at both 25 °C and 600 °C.
Similar high-entropy alloys with high hardness and compressive strength owe those properties to composition- or processing-induced nanoscale phase separation or ordering.
The proposed mechanism is limited to near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi without coarse grains or significant macroscopic phase segregation, under compression from 25 °C to 600 °C.

contradictions.description: The strengthening prediction is conditional on successfully producing nanoscale features, but the stated falsification rule treats simultaneous failure to produce those features and failure to strengthen as falsification. That result would instead show that the intervention did not manipulate the proposed mediator. A decisive falsifier would be successful formation of the specified nanoscale features without the predicted strengthening, under otherwise controlled conditions.
